haiku-low.q1: After the message insert and obx row commit in one txn, the sender gets an ack via GW containing {msg_id, seq}.
haiku-low.q2: Sender sees an error; nobody receives it because no obx row is written and nothing is published. The retry must reuse the same client-generated msg_id, so the stored msg_id/seq is returned with no new row.
haiku-low.q3: After 30 seconds without a heartbeat (clients send one every 10 s), the presence key expires and the user counts as offline. A clean disconnect deletes the key immediately.
haiku-low.q4: G asks the push service to notify the user and leaves the mailbox entry in place. The entry is deleted only when the client acks.
haiku-low.q5: The failure is logged and nothing else happens: there is no retry, and the mailbox row is left untouched.
haiku-low.q6: R1 sets presence, R2 pulls pending entries, R3 loads bodies by msg_id from the DB, R4 sends per conversation in ascending seq, R5 deletes on ack. Live messages during R2-R4 are slotted by seq, and duplicate msg_ids are dropped.
haiku-low.q7: The obx row is committed with the message. The relay or poller deletes it only after the bus confirms the publish, so a crash or bus outage just means later publication, possibly twice.
haiku-low.q8: In an in-memory KV presence cache (online map), mapping user_id to gateway node with a 30 s TTL. The key expires after 30 seconds of silence and is removed.
haiku-low.q9: The dispatcher looks up the online map; if a node G is found, it sends to G's delivery queue. G writes to the socket and starts a 5 s timer, and a client ack within 5 s confirms delivery by deleting the mailbox entry.
haiku-low.q10: In the undelivered-list (pending table), written by the dispatcher before any live attempt, holding pointers only. Entries are removed on client ack or expire after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: It reads the user's pending entries from the pending table, then loads the message bodies by msg_id from the DB.
haiku-low.q12: The bus event is not acked until every recipient is handled, so the bus redelivers it. Another FO instance redoes the whole member list; this is safe because the inbox put is idempotent on (user_id, msg_id).

sonnet.q1: Only after the single transaction (message insert + outbox row) commits. The ack {msg_id, seq} goes back to the sender through the GW; it tells them the message is stored with its msg_id and sequence number.
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error. No outbox row exists, so nothing is published and nobody receives it. The retry must carry the same client-generated msg_id; a resend with it returns the stored msg_id/seq with no new row.
sonnet.q3: After 30 s of silence (no heartbeat; clients send one every 10 s), the presence key's 30 s TTL expires and they count as offline.
sonnet.q4: The socket server (G) asks the push service and leaves the mailbox entry in place (not deleted).
sonnet.q5: The failure is logged and nothing else: no retry, and the mailbox row is untouched.
sonnet.q6: Per conversation in ascending seq order. Duplicate msg_ids are dropped by the client; live messages arriving during reconnect are slotted in by seq.
sonnet.q7: The outbox row is committed in the same transaction as the message, so the relay will still publish it and fanout happens. The client's retry gets the original ack.
sonnet.q8: In the online map / presence cache, an in-memory KV (user_id -> gateway node, TTL 30 s). If the connection dies uncleanly, the TTL expires after 30 s without heartbeat and removes the key.
sonnet.q9: The dispatcher looks up the user's gateway node G in the online map and puts the message on G's delivery queue; G writes it to the socket and starts a 5 s timer. The client's ack within 5 s confirms arrival.
sonnet.q10: In the pending table (mailbox/inbox) of pointers (user_id, conv_id, seq, msg_id), no bodies. It is written by the dispatcher for every recipient before any live delivery attempt. Entries are deleted when the client acks, and they expire after 30 days.
sonnet.q11: It sets presence, reads the user's entries from the pending table, then reads the message bodies by msg_id from the DB.
sonnet.q12: The bus event was not acked, so it is redelivered and another FO/dispatcher instance redoes the whole member list. This is safe because the inbox put is idempotent on (user_id, msg_id) and clients drop duplicate msg_ids.
